clue.text: Judgment with which some disagree? Not half!

definitions.text: Judgment with which some disagree? Not half!

parts.words: Judgment with which some disagree? Not half!
parts.note: a jury's decision reached even though some members dissent, provided the dissenters number fewer than half

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' looks like the British slangy exclamation meaning 'definitely', but read literally it says the dissenters are fewer than half the jury.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury decision accepted when most but not all jurors agree is described this way in courts.

clue.text: Duke's daughter one admitted to male golf club

indicators.note: one piece is let in among the others, as a guest is admitted to a club

parts.note: the R and A (Royal and Ancient) at St Andrews is golf's famous governing club
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A nobleman's daughter becomes the first woman allowed into an all-male golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf club' looks like a stick, but it is the R and A, spelt out as RANDA. In Shakespeare's The Tempest, Prospero, the rightful Duke of Milan, has a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Tempest, Prospero, the deposed Duke of Milan, has this daughter with him on the island.

clue.text: King Henry the writer

definitions.meaning: the name of several kings of England and Scotland, such as the first Stuart king of England
the surname of the American novelist Henry who wrote The Turn of the Screw

explanation.surface: A list of royal and literary Henrys.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs the words together as 'King Henry', but the split is after 'King'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a royal first name borne by Stuart monarchs and the surname of novelist Henry, author of The Ambassadors.

clue.text: Bone in river often found in part of Ireland

indicators.note: the bone goes inside the river-plus-common string, just after its first letter

parts.note: R is the usual abbreviation for river on maps
something often found is common, frequently met with
OS is the Latin and anatomical word for a bone

explanation.surface: A bone discovered in an Irish river is a frequent find.
explanation.walkthrough: ROSCOMMON is a county in the west of the Republic of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the counties of Connacht in the Republic, so it names a region of the island.

clue.text: Follow story on radio

indicators.note: words heard over the airwaves are judged by how they sound, not their spelling

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep up with a serial on the wireless.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone secretly is to trail behind them, a verb also used by detectives.

clue.text: An event I organized? Polo, say

indicators.note: the letters are arranged into a new order, as an event is put together

parts.note: taken as written, letters for the anagram

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have put on a polo match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polo' suggests the horseback sport, but it is Marco Polo, the explorer born in Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo came from Venice, so he is an example of a native of that city.

clue.text: Drive home bishop involved in crash

indicators.note: the bishop is caught up inside the crash, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a crash (financial collapse) is a ruin
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman gets caught up in a car accident on the way home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive home' reads as a journey by car; it means to press a point hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive home a point is to emphasise it insistently, the same as rubbing it in.

clue.text: Form of exaction bringing in millions

definitions.text: Form of exaction bringing in millions

indicators.note: the millions are brought inside the rearranged letters
a new form of the word means its letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A government levy that raises millions of pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is all wordplay and all definition at once: income tax is the state's levy that raises millions, and the rearranged letters of 'exaction' close round the M.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy on earnings is a form of exaction by the state and raises millions for the Treasury.

clue.text: Temporary occupation of the evacuated French city

indicators.note: the word is emptied of its middle, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: Nancy is a city in Lorraine, north-east France

explanation.surface: An occupying army only briefly holding a French city that has been emptied of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuated' empties THE to TE; it looks like part of a wartime picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Renting a property gives the right to occupy it for a fixed period, which is temporary.

clue.text: Operation by army corps brings improvement in patient's condition

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a military operation is a mission

explanation.surface: A military operation leads to a patient getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operation' suggests surgery in this medical picture, but it is a military mission.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease going into abeyance, with symptoms lessening, is the medical sense of this word.

clue.text: Old scientist's post-graduate study

indicators.note: post means after, so the study comes after the graduate

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A scientist of the past did research after his first degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post-graduate' reads as one hyphenated word, but split it: 'post' means after. Roger Bacon, medieval friar, and Francis Bacon, Elizabethan philosopher, both qualify as old scientists.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon, Elizabethan philosopher, and Roger Bacon, medieval friar, were both early scientific thinkers.

clue.text: Wise old king in earnest, originally

indicators.note: the answer sits within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A wise old monarch who was serious in his early days.
explanation.walkthrough: The king of Pylos in Homer's Iliad is the wise elder of the Greeks; he is tucked in earNEST ORiginally.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Iliad this king of Pylos is the venerable counsellor, a byword for an aged sage.

clue.text: He gets shot acting riskily for another

definitions.text: He gets shot acting riskily for another

parts.words: He gets shot acting riskily for another
parts.note: a film double who is filmed performing the dangerous scenes in place of the star

explanation.walkthrough: 'gets shot' suggests a bullet wound but means being filmed by the camera.
explanation.definitionFit: Film professionals who perform dangerous action sequences instead of actors are captured on camera doing so.

clue.text: In celebration

definitions.meaning: being in means being indoors at one's residence
an informal party held in one's own house, where guests are received

explanation.definitionFit: Both the phrase for being indoors at one's residence and the noun for a domestic reception.

clue.text: Person having fixed view from stern on vessel

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: hard means stern, severe
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Someone looks out with a fixed stare from the back of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' suggests the back of a boat beside 'vessel', but it means severe.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uncompromising, who refuses to shift position on an issue, holds an inflexible opinion.

clue.text: Criminal activity of gang I deal with in court

parts.note: a band is a group or gang
taken as written
to try a case is to deal with it in court

explanation.surface: A gang's crimes, which the speaker will handle in a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Robbery by outlaws, especially armed bands, is the activity described as lawless crime.

clue.text: Quickly split up contaminated water in crockery

indicators.note: in a down answer, reading upwards turns the word around

parts.note: to split quickly, leave in a hurry, is to have fled

indicators.note: spoilt water has its letters disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hurriedly breaks up polluted water held in pots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FLED into DELF, and 'contaminated' makes TWARE from WATER. The answer is the blue-and-white earthenware from the Dutch town of Delft.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin-glazed pottery made in the Dutch town of Delft is a type of dishes and pots.

clue.text: Light-hearted little girl broadcasting now

parts.note: Deb is a short form of the girl's name Deborah
a programme going out live is on air

explanation.surface: A cheerful young girl presenting a live programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A carefree, suave and cheerful manner is the meaning of this word, a synonym for jaunty.

clue.text: One moves quickly to attach second peripheral device

parts.note: a printer is a device attached to a computer

explanation.surface: Someone rushes to plug in a second computer accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peripheral device' is computing jargon for an add-on such as a printer.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete who runs short races at full speed is a fast mover.

clue.text: Exercise for working on stomach and on posterior

parts.note: a sit-up is an exercise for the stomach muscles
taken as written

explanation.surface: A workout routine for the abdomen and the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial term for the part of the body you sit on, the bottom, is a jocular name for the buttocks.

clue.text: King careless about source of warning

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
lax means careless
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A lax monarch is unconcerned about where an alert came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a container signal here but simply means ON (concerning).
explanation.definitionFit: This loud electric horn, once fitted to cars, sounds an alert.

clue.text: He's too close, so coach and trap get overturned

indicators.note: in a down answer the coach and trap are turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a drag is a private four-horse coach
a gin is a snare or trap for game

explanation.surface: A carriage driver in a crash: his coach and pony trap overturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach and trap' paint horse-drawn vehicles, but the trap is a gin. 'get overturned' turns DRAGGIN round. 'close' means mean with money.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser, someone stingy or tight-fisted, is close with money in the old sense.

clue.text: Programme based on cheap material?

parts.note: a broadcast built on conversation, which the saying holds is cheap

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'talk is cheap' is the key: a chat-based broadcast is made from cheap stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast of interviews and chat is made from conversation, the cheapest of materials.

clue.text: Cut something between a month and a year

definitions.meaning: a cut or gash, as with a blade

definitions.text: something between a month and a year
definitions.meaning: the stroke written between month and year in a date such as 6/99

explanation.definitionFit: Both a sweeping cut and the oblique stroke separating figures in a written date.

clue.text: Fraud surrounding monarch's succession

indicators.note: the fraud goes round the monarch, enclosing it

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick or fraud
R stands for Rex or Regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A scam involving who inherits the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succession' looks royal beside 'monarch', but it means a series.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of things one after another, such as a run of wins, is a sequence.

clue.text: Help 28 after rising in Republic

indicators.note: in a down answer the letters go upwards, so they read backwards

parts.note: aid is help
the answer to 28 across is the province abbreviated NI

explanation.surface: A helper rising in a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns AIDNI into INDIA. 28 refers to the answer at 28 across, the province usually written NI.
explanation.definitionFit: This South Asian nation became a republic in 1950.

clue.text: Capital invested by British, say, in food store

indicators.note: the word is judged by how it is pronounced

parts.note: Delhi, India's capital, was besieged by British forces in 1857

explanation.surface: Britons putting money into a grocery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' suggests money, but to invest a city is to besiege it: the British besieged Delhi in 1857, and DELHI is said like DELI.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen, shortened, is a shop selling prepared foods and cooked meats.

clue.text: Exotic animal seen in parts of Pennsylvania, briefly

definitions.text: Exotic animal seen in parts of Pennsylvania, briefly

parts.words: Exotic animal seen in parts of Pennsylvania, briefly
parts.note: Pennsylvania shortened is PA, and its two parts, said as a phrase, name a Chinese bear

explanation.surface: A rare creature spotted in some regions of Pennsylvania.
explanation.walkthrough: Pennsylvania's abbreviation is PA; its parts are P and A, which run together spell an animal. 'Exotic animal' is the definition and the rest is a letter game the grammar has no single op for.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-white bear of China is an animal from far away for western zoo visitors.

clue.text: Tsarina I expelled from Mediterranean port

indicators.note: the letter is thrown out of the word, as someone is expelled from a place

parts.note: Alexandria is Egypt's great Mediterranean port

explanation.surface: An empress throwing the speaker out of a Mediterranean harbour city.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexandra was the last Tsarina, wife of Nicholas II of Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of Tsar Nicholas II, Russia's last empress, bore this first name.

clue.text: Down with five others in province

definitions.text: Down with five others in province

parts.words: Down with five others in province
parts.note: County Down together with five more counties makes up a UK province

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' is not a direction or a mood but County Down; the province has six counties.
explanation.definitionFit: The six counties, including Down, Antrim and Armagh, together make up this UK region.
